summary.intent: Make the Ask Soony buyer-inbox app more compelling for a hackathon demo: add automatic n8n-style visualization of agent-written routines for no-coders, and rethink the whole UI (world map, top bar, visual style) from top to bottom.
summary.outcome: Backend work finished: 7 real demo cards, activity 'via' source tracking, a voice 'teach_routine' tool that drafts a switched-off routine, and a demo reset script, with 181 tests passing. The flow-view brief was extended for the Routines builder, and three parallel design agents were launched for the UI redesign; the final layout was not yet chosen or built.

repo: Agent-generated routines are structured recipes (conditions -> steps -> fixed brake), which is what makes automatic flow-chart rendering possible without manual modelling.
Routine drafts created by voice are stored switched off in routine_drafts.json keyed by card id and exposed via GET /api/routines/drafts; they are never auto-enabled.
scripts/demo_cards.py hardcodes only document references; quantities, prices, dates and addresses are read from the portal at run time, and it checks PDFs still contain the expected text.

demo_cards.py merges entries by id so reruns are idempotent; --reset backs up state files as <name>.before-demo-<timestamp>.json, clears decision/action/reply/teams/draft state and switches all routines off.
Card deadlines are set to 10:00 or 12:00 launch day but at least 1-3 hours after the script runs, so they go overdue; the script must be rerun shortly before the demo.
--reset writes teams_posted.json as an empty list, so a configured Teams webhook will repost all open red and amber cards once.
Files like web/src/lib/api.ts and Routines.tsx belong to teammates, and the world map view is Akshat's work, so changes there need coordination.

code.finding: build_activity, escalate and dismiss now record a 'via' source (voice/routine/inbox), taken from the card's action_id action or latest action, defaulting to 'inbox'.
Voice escalate/reject pass via 'voice'; new teach_routine tool refuses open cards ('decide first') and sends a 'Routine draft ready' push in try/except.
Hang-up delay after goodbye raised from 0.8s to 4s and cancelled if the buyer speaks or a tool runs, so the user can say 'next time just do that'.

workflow: Parallel background subagents (backend builder, Routines builder, design agents) with task notifications and SendMessage for passing follow-up wiring tasks.
Screenshots were reviewed to judge UI quality before deciding on redesign.
For ambiguous design direction the user preferred fanning out several design subagents and then building the best combination rather than choosing up front.

friction: The user's 'visualize the code' question was first read narrowly, and they had to clarify they meant the overall UI top to bottom.
The backend hang-up timing in VoiceCall.tsx blocked the 'next time just do that' voice flow and had to be changed.
Frontend wiring for activity[].via and the drafts endpoint sits in teammates' files, so the backend builder couldn't complete the end-to-end feature.
open_items: Frontend must display activity[].via and read GET /api/routines/drafts (web/src/lib/api.ts and Routines.tsx, teammate-owned).
Routines builder still implementing the n8n-style Flow | Steps view with last-run counters and the non-removable brake node.
Choose and build the final UI layout from the three design agent proposals (launch timeline instead of world map, map as 'Suppliers' tab), coordinating with Akshat.
Run a final review, check tests, and commit; nothing is committed yet.
Decide whether --reset should delete teams_posted.json instead of writing an empty list to avoid a Teams repost.
Rerun demo_cards.py or --reset shortly before the demo so deadlines are not overdue.
